st.t: Photo Gallery of HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj's Vicharan, Photo Story
w: We present a photo essay of Swamishri visiting the dying Prabhudas Lalaji - a bona fide devotee from the time of Shastriji Maharaj. Swamishri blesses, prays and appreciates his devotion.

Birth is an occasion of joy and celebration, and death is an occasion of loss and mourning. In Hinduism, life is a cycle of births and deaths. The journey of an individual's life is punctuated with 16 Samskars (sacraments), beginning with birth and ending in death. Each samskar seeks to elevate the individual emotionally, morally and spiritually. The final rite is the death rite. Death is seen as the changing of clothes and the wearing of another (Gita 2:22), where the soul transmigrates into another body until it realises God. Hinduism does not see death as the end, but theologically as an opportunity for the soul to free itself from the fetters of maya and finally savour the eternal divine bliss of God. A pious individual, no matter how he or she dies, but by virtue of his or her lifelong devotion and dedication to God or the Gunatit Sadhu attains the abode of God. So the death of a bhakta or devotee is undoubtedly an occasion of mourning because such a great soul has departed from our midst, and on the other hand it is a divine event because he has accomplished the final goal of life - moksha - and has become eternally happy. On such occasions the divine form of God and the Gunatit Sadhu arrive to take his soul to their abode.

Prabhudas Lalaji was a dedicated and enthusiastic devotee who had inherited satsang from his parents. In 1927 he went to Uganda, but due to his ailing business he returned back to India in 1948. However, on meeting Shastriji Maharaj, he returned back to Uganda on his instruction. He returned again to India to celebrate the 75th birthday (Suvarna Jayanti) of Shastriji Maharaj in Atladra. At that time Swami initially told him to donate Rs.5,000, then increased the amount to Rs.10,000 and finally Rs.15,000. Though Prabhudasbhai did not have the means, he buoyantly promised to do so. On hearing this, Maganbhai of Africa congratulated Prabhudasbhai for not refusing despite his penury. Subsequently, Maganbhai and other devotees collected the money and donated it to Shastriji Maharaj on behalf of the E. Africa Satsang Mandal.

Shastriji Maharaj had also blessed Prabhudas Lalaji with a canvas murti of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj and Bhagatji Maharaj; and after performing the arti he instructed him to keep the murtis in his house and perform puja daily. The weekly Satsang assembly was held in his house from 1948 to 1960 till Yogiji Maharaj consecrated a mandir in Kampala.

When Yogiji Maharaj visited Kampala in 1970, he asked for the murti of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj blessed by Shastriji Maharaj; which he subsequently consecrated in the first Swaminarayan Mandir in Islington, London . (The same murti was then installed in Ashton-U-Lyne in 1974)

In 1972, when Idi Amin expelled the Indians from Uganda, Prabhudas Lalaji returned to India. His enthusiasm never ebbed despite returning empty-handed. When people sympathized about his loss he would say with pride, "I had gone wearing a dhoti and returned donned in a pant and shirt." From thenceforth he attended festivals, travelled to villages and inspired satsang in people through his discourses. He stayed in Vidyanagar and visited the Chhatralay for daily darshan and discourses.

A few years ago he was afflicted with sciatica, causing severe pain to his legs. On informing Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Swamishri blessed him and said, "Maharaj will cure your ailment." And from then onwards Prabhudasbhai recovered.
On 25 July, Swamishri personally blessed and prayed for the unconscious Prabhudas Lalaji and on 29 July 2001 he passed away to forever stay in the service of Maharaj and Swami in Akshardham.

Kishore - Kishori Din On Kishore-Kishori Day in Houston, members of the Southwest Kishore Mandal highlighted several qualities of Bhagwan Swaminarayan, the guru parampara, and Swamishri through a special awards ceremony.

Finally, kishores offered various awards to Swamishri, while explaining in detail the reasons why he should be recognised as 'Adarsh Shishya', 'Seva Murti', 'Bhakti Swarup', 'Aham Shunya Purush', and 'Param Hitkari Sant'. As part of the awards ceremony, during the presentation of the Adarsh Shishya Award, Swamishri was asked to explicate verses from the Bhaktachintamani and narrate an incident in which he gave up his own desires to follow his guru Shastriji Maharaj's wishes.

ds.t: In satsang we must stay united
w: Friday, 29 July 2005 (Ashadh vad 9, Samvat 2061), Bochasan

There was ill feeling between two devotees. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had them stand before him, because on account of these two devotees there was a serious rift between their sons as well. Swamishri asked, "What is the reason for the ill feeling?"

"There is no other reason. It happened because of a mocham." (In the Kanam region, ill feeling that arises over the right of way between two pieces of land sharing a common boundary is called mocham.)
Swamishri understood immediately. Swamishri said, "There was a problem about the field and there was abuse, but now is that problem over or not?"
"It is over now."

"If that problem is over, then settle this too today. In satsang we must stay united. If there is quarrelling with one another in satsang, we do not get the joy of satsang, and satsang does not grow either. So from today give up this ill feeling and start speaking to each other." Swamishri struck an axe at the quarrel that had taken root.

As the talk went on in this way, C. M. Kaka of London was mentioned, and Swamishri, singing his glory, said, "C. M. was very jolly, very sociable. He mixed with everyone and always spoke with a smile."
"When C. M. passed away to Akshardham, you were very grieved," said Bhagwatcharan Swami.

Swamishri said, "How could one not grieve? What a devotee he was! What work he did for the Tororo mandir! He brought the murtis at the risk of his life, and after going to London he did not do any worldly business at all. He did only the mandir's work. His constant thought was how to collect funds and donations. Whatever he said, everyone took it to heart, and being from Nar, he was never at a loss for words. Such a devotee he was." Quite naturally Swamishri described the glory of one close to him and inspired everyone to understand the glory of devotees.

Swamishri performed the pratishtha rituals of Shri Sita-Ram Dev and Hanumanji and Shri Shankar-Parvatiji and Ganapatiji besides the presiding murtis of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj and Shri Radha-Krishna Dev. At 7.00 pm Swamishri arrived at the Expo centre. The assembly theme of “He gurudev, apna anant chhe upakar” was elaborated upon with speeches by Tyagvallabh Swami, Ishwarcharan Swami, Viveksagar Swami, Anandswarup Swami and Gnaneshwar Swami. On Swamishri’s arrival a cultural dance was performed by youths. Thereafter senior sadhus garlanded and offered shawls to Swamishri. Then Swamishri blessed the assembly, “A guru reveals true knowledge and direction in life. Through him we realize God, his true glory and the realization of one’s atma. God has blessed us with this human body to realize the true knowledge of atma. “The more your expectations and desires, the more your problems. You should earn as much as you need and also donate for the welfare of others… The essence of all shastras is that one attains moksha through God or his Sadhu.” Finally Swamishri blessed all with samip darshan.

On the day of Guru Purnima some teenagers asked Swamishri, “You had pleased Shastriji Maharaj, similarly, bless us so that we can please you.” Swamishri posed a question, “You all live in America?” “Yes.” “Then remain steadfast in Satsang. Don’t spend your money in bad habits. Don’t eat outside (in restaurants, etc.). Regularly attend the weekly satsang assembly and participate in satsang activities. Don’t watch bad things on television – if you follow this then I will be happy upon you.”

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and Guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages or other devotional means. The spiritual endeavors performed by the devotees during Swamishri's visit to the local centers are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. It also reflects Swamishri's divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.

How to transcend the three states

28 July 2010, Bochasan A South Indian aspirant enquired of Swamishri, “What is the path to transcend the three states (of waking, dream and deep sleep)?” Swamishri replied briefly, “God’s refuge ( ashro ). Daily do mala and pray to him.”

A man had come with his son. This son had fallen into the company of the sons of hooligans and was surrounded by all kinds of vices. He had good sanskars in childhood, but in his youth, because of bad company, he had started extorting money from people of modest means, such as rickshaw drivers. After extorting money from such people, if a complaint was made, the son of a police officer would get him released. In such a gang he had forgotten his sense of duty. His parents were unhappy because of his shameful behaviour day after day. Moreover, because of him, a question mark had arisen over his elder brother's marriage of ten years. His behaviour was also getting in the way of the marriage of his only sister. In this family of modest means, it was as if the son had come as a disaster. His mother, surrounded by problems, had even prepared to go to the Tapi river and throw herself in. However, because she had heard the words of satsang, she gave up that step, persuaded her son and sent him to Swamishri.

Swamishri listened to the whole story and lovingly explained to the boy, "Think about it. How many people are unhappy because of you!? Everyone is pained because of you, so mend your ways. Rather than all these people being unhappy, mend your ways and be happy! Be careful, life is ruined in such bad company. Do puja regularly, and also go to the satsang assembly."
After just a few of Swamishri's loving, selfless words, that youth gave his word to change his life. A family was saved.

A man had come with his son. This son had fallen in with the sons of street thugs and was surrounded by many kinds of vices. He had good values in childhood, but in his youth, because of bad company, he had begun extorting money from people of ordinary means such as rickshaw drivers. If a complaint was made after extorting money from such people, a police officer's son would get them released. In such a gang he had forgotten all sense of duty. His parents were unhappy because of his daily outrageous behaviour. Moreover, because of him, even his elder brother's ten year old marriage had come into question. His behaviour was also getting in the way of his only sister's marriage. In this family of ordinary means, it was as if the son had come as a calamity, and his mother, surrounded by problems, had even prepared to go to the Tapi and throw herself in. But because she had heard the words of satsang, she gave up that step, persuaded her son and sent him to Swamishri.

Swamishri listened to the whole story and lovingly explained to the boy, "Think about it. How many people are unhappy because of you!? Everyone is pained on your account, so mend your ways. Rather than all of them being unhappy, mend your ways and be happy! Be careful, life is ruined in such bad company. Do puja regularly, and also go to the satsang assembly."
With just a few affectionate, selfless words from Swamishri, that young man promised to change his life. A family was saved.
